title: Experiments of methane gas solubility in formation water under high temperature and high pressure and their geological significance
experimental_method: Ultra-high-pressure PVT cell with sapphire window and stirring; after 2 h stirring and 4 h rest, liquid and gas samples withdrawn at constant pressure and flashed at ambient conditions; gas volume measured in a gas meter (0.01 mL), condensed water and degassed liquid weighed (0.01 g).
quality_remarks: Liquid is a 0.23 mol/kg NaHCO3 solution (density 1.0116 g/cm3) mimicking South China Sea formation water, not pure water or NaCl brine. Solubility unit m3/m3 at STP (273.2 K, 0.10 MPa) with the denominator volume undefined. Paper states solubility in formation water is below the Duan and Mao (2006) model and below Blount and Price pure-water data; water content in gas agrees with Olds et al. (1942) at low pressure. Methane purity over 99.99 %. The solubility values rise monotonically with T from 353 K, unlike the usual minimum near 350 K in pure water; they are listed to only three significant figures.
